chapter: Miles Davis stories and what jazz means
title: Mothers forbidding the blues and rag
summary: Gil and Johnston recall Black mothers who forbade blues or rag at home, with Eubie Blake's experience.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: White people, well black people too are ...........(VOICE FADES OUT). I had a friend and they were jamming at his house, and his mother wouldn't allow him to play the blues. And that was a black woman.

Well I've heard Eubie Blake say more than once that he was playing on the organ in his house and his mother said, don't play that rag in my house. And he said that was the first time that he'd ever heard the word.
And another thing, so much is made now of

the bands that used to go to and from the cemetery. And although New Orleans gets credit for it, the same thing was happening in other places. It certainly happened in Baltimore. And he said that these are the people, so called decent people, never followed those bands.
He said, only the worst kinds of people did. And that his mother positively forbade him to follow them. But of course, they were irresistible for him, you see. (LAUGHTER).
